audience: the City of Marlow's finance committee
decision: which department to put under a mid-year spending review

columns.annual_budget_k: approved budget for the year, $ thousands
columns.spent_to_date_k: spent from January to July, $ thousands
columns.committed_k: ordered but not yet paid, $ thousands
columns.forecast_year_end_k: forecast spending for the full year, $ thousands
columns.variance_pct: variance as a percentage of budget

findings.text: Police has the largest budget, $42.0 million.
The city forecasts a $4.8 million overspend for the year. Transit accounts for $3.1 million of it (65%); Roads ($0.8 million) and Police ($0.6 million) are next.
Contracts are under budget in 7 of 10 departments, mostly because invoices arrive late in the year.
Spending to date is 60% of the annual budget after 7 of 12 months (58% would be on track).
Parks has the largest underspend, $0.4 million.
The Roads forecast assumes snow clearing at the five-year average. A harsh winter could add up to $1.5 million to Roads' overspend.
Fire's overtime forecast is 12% above last year's actual but still within its budget.
Most of Transit's overspend is overtime: $2.4 million over a $2.0 million overtime budget (+120%), from driver vacancies covered by extra shifts.
IT's $0.3 million overspend comes from software licence renewals.

main.gist: Transit drives most of the city's overspend (mostly overtime)

caveat.gist: A harsh winter could add up to $1.5 million to Roads
